# DEPTH Therapy — Lorne Lieberman, LMFT

> Private-pay psychotherapy practice in Los Feliz, Los Angeles, California, with secure telehealth for clients anywhere in California. Depth-oriented individual therapy, couples therapy, and trauma & EMDR therapy with Lorne Lieberman, a Licensed Marriage and Family Therapist (California LMFT #159526).

## Practice facts
- Practice name: DEPTH Therapy (formerly Now Here Therapy; legal: Lorne Matthew Lieberman, LMFT, dba Now Here Therapy)
- Therapist: Lorne Lieberman, LMFT — Licensed Marriage & Family Therapist, California LMFT #159526
- Credentials: EMDR Trained through an EMDRIA-approved program (December 2025); Gottman Method Trained (2025); Relational Gestalt Trained (2023)
- Education: M.A., Clinical Psychology, Antioch University Los Angeles (2023); B.A., Psychology, Summa Cum Laude, CUNY School of Professional Studies (2020)
- Experience: three years as a suicide and crisis hotline counselor
- Offices (Los Feliz): 1708 Hillhurst Ave., Los Angeles, CA 90027; and Wellness Spaces Los Feliz, 2150 Hillhurst Ave., Los Angeles, CA 90027
- Telehealth: secure Zoom video for clients located anywhere in California
- Phone: (323) 505-9006

- Booking: free 15-minute phone consultation at https://depth.la/contact/

## Services and fees
- Individual therapy: $250 per 55-minute session
- Couples therapy: $300 per 55-minute session
- Extended 90-minute (double) session, individual or couples: $500
- Initial phone consultation: free, 15 minutes
- Payment: private pay; monthly superbills provided for clients with out-of-network benefits

## Approach
Depth-oriented, relational psychotherapy anchored in Relational Gestalt and relational psychoanalysis, integrating EMDR, the Gottman Method, attachment-informed somatic emotional processing, and mindfulness-based Buddhist psychology. Lorne grew up in a Los Angeles film and television family (his late father was a film and TV director), spent half his life working in film and the creative arts, and spent over a decade living as a renunciate Buddhist monk before becoming a therapist. He works with adults and couples, including artists, performers, and entertainment-industry professionals, seeking long-term, in-depth work.
